messages.content: I think my family has a pattern of not talking about problems until they explode.
Honestly, that's a really common family dynamic, and it's genuinely hard to break individually. What made you notice the pattern this time?
A small disagreement turned into a huge blowout about things from years ago.
That's honestly classic pressure-cooker dynamics - unaddressed stuff builds quietly until a small trigger releases all of it at once.
Is there anything I can actually do differently as just one person in the family?
Honestly, you can model addressing things earlier yourself, even if others don't follow immediately - it won't fix the whole pattern alone, but it's a real starting point.
